step1_analysis.circuit_type: Broadband Differential Amplifier / Darlington-type VCO Delay Cell
step1_analysis.description: A high-speed differential amplifier utilizing a modified Darlington topology with emitter follower inputs and cascode stages. It is designed to provide wide bandwidth and is likely used as a delay cell in the Darlington-type voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) mentioned in the paper.

paper_reference.title: A 39-to-45-Gbit/s Multi-Data-Rate Clock and Data Recovery Circuit With a Robust Lock Detector

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifier stage.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly reported for this single cell

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a tail current of 2-5mA from a 1.8V supply for high-speed operation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High-speed CML/bipolar-style logic requires significant static current to drive parasitic capacitances at high frequencies.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ gm * R_load. With R_load=500Ω and gm=20mA/V, gain is around 10 V/V (20 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: VCO delay cells typically need a moderate gain (>1 V/V at oscillation frequency) to ensure startup and maintain oscillation.

bandwidth_3db.description: The frequency at which the differential gain drops by 3 dB from its DC value.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant at the output node. BW ≈ 1 / (2 * pi * R_load * C_out).
sky130_expected.reasoning: While the original InP HBT process achieves >40 GHz, a generic NPN or SKY130 equivalent would likely yield a lower bandwidth in the 10-20 GHz range without heavy inductive peaking.

transient_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output nodes during high-speed operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Swing = I_tail * R_load. If I_tail = 2mA and R_load = 500Ω, swing is 1V single-ended.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CML and bipolar logic typically operate with reduced swings (200mV - 500mV) to maximize speed and keep transistors out of deep saturation.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC bandwidth, DC gain, and transient voltage swing of the Darlington-type delay cell.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Darlington-type Broadband Amplifier Testbench

* Generic NPN model for simulation since the netlist uses 'npn'
.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100 tf=5p cje=20f cjc=20f)

* DUT (Resistor values appended for simulation)
R1 n1 label_net_0 500
R2 n12 GND 1k
R3 n2 GND 1k
R4 n9 GND 1k
R5 n3 label_net_1 500
R6 n5 label_net_2 1k
Q1 n7 n9 n0 npn
Q2 label_net_3 label_net_4 n2 npn
R7 n4 GND 1k
R8 n8 label_net_5 1k
Q3 n3 n2 n9 npn
R9 label_net_7 GND 1k
Q4 n0 label_net_8 GND npn
Q5 n10 n10 n8 npn
Q6 n3 n10 n7 npn
Q7 n1 n10 n6 npn
Q8 n10 n10 n12 npn
Q9 n1 n4 n5 npn
Q10 n6 n5 n0 npn
Q11 label_net_10 label_net_11 n4 npn

* Power Supplies (1.8V)
VCC0 label_net_0 0 1.8
VCC1 label_net_1 0 1.8
VCC3 label_net_3 0 1.8
VCC5 label_net_5 0 1.8
VCC10 label_net_10 0 1.8

* Ground Connections
VGND2 label_net_2 0 0
VGND7 label_net_7 0 0

* Bias Voltage
VBIAS label_net_8 0 0.9

* Differential Inputs (DC=1.2V, AC=1V, Tran=5GHz sine)
VINP label_net_4 0 dc 1.2 ac 1 sin(1.2 0.1 5G)
VINN label_net_11 0 dc 1.2 ac -1 sin(1.2 -0.1 5G)

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let total_current = -(i(VCC0) + i(VCC1) + i(VCC3) + i(VCC5) + i(VCC10))
let power = total_current * 1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 20 1Meg 100G
let vout_diff = v(n3) - v(n1)
let gain_db = vdb(vout_diff)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1Meg
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=(dc_gain-3) fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis for Voltage Swing
tran 2p 2n
meas tran vout_pp_p pp v(n3)
meas tran vout_pp_n pp v(n1)
let vout_diff_tran = v(n3) - v(n1)
meas tran vout_diff_pp pp vout_diff_tran

quit
.endc
.end
